title: Measure
summary: A measure assigns a nonnegative size to measurable sets while adding the sizes of disjoint pieces.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared measure theory context is fixed.

content.plain: A measure assigns a nonnegative size to measurable sets while adding the sizes of disjoint pieces.
content.exact: For a measurable space (Ω,𝓕), μ:𝓕→[0,∞] is a measure when μ(∅)=0 and μ(⋃ₙAₙ)=Σₙμ(Aₙ) for every pairwise-disjoint sequence (Aₙ).
content.example: Length on intervals extends to Lebesgue measure on a sigma-algebra of subsets of the real line.
content.caveat: A measure needs a declared measurable space; assigning a size to every conceivable subset may be impossible or undesirable.
